To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the base excision and mismatch repair pathways cooperate in active demethylation.
the mismatch repair (MMR) pathway can participate in the removal of oxidized bases and 5-methyl cytosine (5 mC) from DNA.

1) the base excision and mismatch repair pathways cooperate in the removal of closely spaced oxidative and methylated DNA lesions in mammalian cells; 2) the mismatch repair pathway can process multiple mispairs in mammalian cells and this process is promoted by the presence of base excision repair-generated nicks; and 3) the mismatch repair and base excision repair pathways cooperate in active DNA demethylations in mammalian cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of DNA repair pathways in active demethylation of mammalian DNA.
understanding the role of DNA repair pathways in the regulation of epigenetic processes.
the role of BER and ncMMRs in the processing of oxidative base lesions and 5mC during active demethylation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
both BER and ncMMRs can be used to process 5mC lesions, and the choice of the repair pathway depends on the type of the lesion and the cellular context.
ncMMR and short-patch BER cooperate in ADDM, whereas long-patch BER can also participate in the repair of 5mC lesions.
both the BER pathway and the ncMMR pathway are involved in the active removal of oxidized DNA bases during the active demethylation of CpG sites.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in addition of short-patch BER and long-patch DNA BER, ncMMR can also participate in the processing of 5hmC and 5mC in mammalian cells, which might be important during ADDM.
ncMMR can process oxidized bases and methylcytosine in mammalian cells, which may be important in the removal of toxic BER intermediaries in ADDM.
ncMMR can process multiple oxidative lesions and 5mC in the same DNA molecule.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the BER pathway is not the only pathway that participates in ADDM and that ncMMR can be involved in the process.
ncMMR can process oxidative base damage and 5mC lesions, and that it can be activated by BER-mediated DNA nicking in mammalian cells.
the BER and MMR pathways cooperate in the removal of oxidative and alkylated DNA base lesions, and that this cooperation might be important in active DNA demethyltion.
